text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Director of Kenya Wildlife Service David Western says the agency will support wildlife hunting on private land on an experimental basis.
- Teachers in the country's 41 technical institutes will benefit from a new scheme of service which gives them salary increases ranging from 13 to 17 percent.
- The chairman of the tiny opposition Kenya National Congress party Chibule wa Tsuma is ousted.
- Kenya Cooperative Creameries says it will import butter to supplement dwindling stock.
- The chairman of beach hotels Security Task Force says police will be deployed at various tourist drop points to stop harassment of tourists by freelance tour guides.
- A total of 14,390 people have died in road accidents in the last three years.
- Kenyan police release a description of the stowaway youth who died in a British Airways aircraft to members of the public for identification.
- The government dispatches military helicopters to beef up security in the Eastern district of Marsabit where 36 people were massacred.
